item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft SharePoint Online: Classic publishing restrictions begin March 1, 2027
item.description:
[What and why]

As previously announced in MC1464926, we are introducing restrictions on classic publishing and custom scripting in SharePoint Online to reduce security and governance risks associated with legacy customization. Beginning March 1, 2027, we will block the creation of new classic publishing sites and the activation of publishing features for site collections and subsites across all tenants. Administrators will no longer be able to override these restrictions using the AllowClassicPublishingSiteCreation tenant setting.

This reminder outlines the changes taking effect on March 1, 2027, and the steps administrators should take to prepare.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Rollout will begin in early March 2027 and is expected to complete by early October 2028.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • All SharePoint Online tenants.
  • Administrators managing classic publishing sites, custom scripts, provisioning automation, and migration workflows.
  • Tenants created on or after March 1, 2027, which will have additional restrictions.

Platforms and services

  • SharePoint Online

What will happen

All tenants, beginning March 1, 2027:

  • SharePoint Online will block the creation of classic publishing sites and the activation of publishing features for site collections and subsites.
  • SharePoint Online will enforce the AllowClassicPublishingSiteCreation tenant setting as False. Administrators will no longer be able to change this setting.

Additional restrictions for tenants created on or after March 1, 2027:

  • Users will no longer be able to create or edit classic user-created pages or add or update custom scripts.
  • SharePoint Online will enforce the DenyAddAndCustomizePages site setting as True. Administrators will no longer be able to change this setting.
  • The Allow users to create new modern pages setting in SharePoint admin center > Settings > Pages will be enabled and cannot be disabled.
  • This modern-page setting change will not affect existing tenants.

Classic user-created pages in scope:

  • Affected pages include wiki, Web Part, blog, publishing, and custom ASPX pages.
  • List and library views and list form pages are excluded from the page read-only change.
  • Custom scripts embedded in these experiences will remain subject to scripting restrictions when the applicable phase takes effect.

[Action required and recommendations]

Before March 1, 2027:

  • Identify provisioning automation and migration plans that create classic publishing site collections or subsites or activate publishing features.
  • Update affected workflows to use modern alternatives.

To prepare for October 1, 2028, we recommend that existing tenants:

  • Review the requirements for the classic pages assessment.
  • Inventory classic pages using the Microsoft 365 Assessment Tool and assign modernization owners.
  • Pilot the transformation of classic SharePoint pages to modern pages. Transformation approaches vary by page type, and customized pages may require rebuilding.

[Learn more]

  • Requirements for the classic pages assessment | Microsoft Learn
  • Transform classic SharePoint pages to modern pages | Microsoft Learn

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Entra: Choose your own telephony provider now generally available
item.description:
Updated November 23, 2026: Bring Your Own Telephony (BYOT) is now generally available. We've updated this post with BYOT details.

Updated October 30, 2026: We have updated this post with additional information as the feature is now generally available. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

Choose Your Own Telephony Provider (CYOT) and Bring Your Own Telephony Provider (BYOT) are now generally available in Microsoft Entra ID. Both connect Microsoft Entra to a telephony provider through an integration in your Azure subscription, but you purchase and deploy them differently. Microsoft Entra continues to manage the authentication experience, including one-time passcode (OTP) generation and validation, and your provider delivers the SMS messages and voice calls. 

  • CYOT is the recommended option when a supported offering meets your coverage, contractual and compliance requirements. It gives you providers evaluated by Microsoft for geographic coverage and fraud protection, purchasing through Microsoft Security Store, billing through your Azure subscription and guided deployment in the Microsoft Entra admin center. 
  • BYOT is for cases where an existing provider agreement or a specific requirement can't be met by the supported CYOT offerings. You get your provider's ready-to-deploy integration package, set up your account directly with the provider, and configure the integration through APIs. 

With either option, your organization owns the Azure resources in your subscription and your telephony provider account. 

Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication starts retiring on February 1, 2027. If your users need SMS or voice after that date, set up CYOT or BYOT before then. 

Microsoft recommends phishing-resistant authentication methods, such as passkeys, instead of SMS or voice. Use a telephony provider only for user groups that have a business, regulatory or technical need for telephony-based authentication.

[What you need to do]

If your organization needs to keep SMS or voice authentication: 

  1. Identify users who need SMS or voice. Confirm which users have a requirement that phishing-resistant methods can't meet. 
  2. Choose your option and provider. Review CYOT and BYOT. Use CYOT when a supported provider meets your coverage, contractual and compliance requirements. Otherwise, use BYOT. 
  3. Check prerequisites. You need an Azure subscription with a valid payment method to host the integration, plus the Owner role or Contributor plus Role Based Access Control Administrator. For CYOT, the subscription must also be eligible for Security Store purchases. 
  4. Estimate costs. Review provider pricing and Azure hosting costs. 
  5. Set up and roll out. Follow the setup guide for CYOT or BYOT. Start in evaluation mode, then move traffic to your provider in stages. 
  6. Complete your transition before February 1, 2027. Review the guidance for the retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication.

Learn more 

  • Choose your own telephony provider for SMS and voice authentication 
  • Set up SMS and voice with your own telecom provider 
  • Troubleshoot SMS and voice 
  • Protect against telephony fraud 
  • Plan for resiliency and high availability 
  • Frequently asked questions 
  • Passkeys by default and retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Outlook for iOS/Android: Improved Contacts with profile enrichment and duplicate management
item.description:
Updated November 23, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience.

We’re enhancing the contact experience in Microsoft Outlook Mobile (iOS and Android) by introducing profile-enriched contacts and automatic duplicate contact management. These improvements aim to streamline contact views and provide richer organizational context.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 493753.

This feature has previously been released to the People Hub in new Outlook for Windows. More details in MC927963 (Updated) New Microsoft Outlook for Windows: People Hub improvements (published November 2024, updated April 2025).

[When this will happen:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out mid-July 2025 (previously late June) and expect to complete by end of March 2027 (previously mid-November 2026).

[How this will affect your organization:]

Before this rollout, Outlook Mobile may have displayed multiple entries for the same contact and lacked organizational profile context.

After this rollout:

  • Contacts will be unified into a single enriched view, displaying additional profile information from your organization’s directory (where available).
  • Identical duplicate contacts will be automatically hidden.
  • These enhancements will be on by default and apply to both iOS and Android versions of Outlook Mobile. No admin controls exist.
  • Users can access their contact list by selecting Contacts from the Apps section in the Outlook Mobile app.

[What you need to do to prepare:]

This rollout will happen automatically by the specified dates with no admin action required before the rollout. You may want to notify your users about this change and update internal documentation.

After the feature is rolled out, please ensure that users have updated to the latest version of Outlook for iOS or Outlook for Android.

Learn more: Manage Outlook contacts in your organization - Microsoft Support

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Migrate Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing before EWS deprecation
item.description:
Updated November 23, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Gov rollout of this feature is still paused at this time. We will communicate via Message center when we are ready to proceed. We apologize for any inconvenience.

[What and Why:]

Exchange Web Services (EWS) deprecation begins October 1, 2026. Cross-tenant collaboration features — Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing — currently rely on EWS.

Cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips will be available by September 2026 and Calendar Sharing will be available by early December 2026 (previously late November) via Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy, which replaces EWS-based cross-tenant collaboration.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Worldwide: We will begin rolling out in August 2026 and expect to complete by September 15, 2026 for Free/Busy, Mailtips and December 4, 2026 (previously November 23) for Calendar Sharing.
  • GCC, GCC High, DoD: We will communicate via Message center when we are ready to proceed.

[Impact on your organization:]

Sharing Free/Busy, Calendars, and MailTips (e.g., out of office message) with another Microsoft 365 organization via Organization Relationship or Sharing Policy relies on Exchange Web Services (EWS), which is being deprecated. To preserve these cross-tenant collaboration scenarios, you will need to start migrating to Microsoft 365 Cross Tenant Access Policy.

Your tenant is affected if it uses any of the following Exchange Online configurations:

  • Organization Relationships — sharing Free/Busy or MailTips with other Microsoft 365 tenants 
  • Sharing Policies — sharing calendars externally, either via invitations sent to recipients in other Microsoft 365 organizations or calendars published for anonymous access via an internet URL

Run these commands in Exchange Online PowerShell to check if your tenant is affected: 

    • Get-OrganizationRelationship | Format-List Name, DomainNames, Enabled, FreeBusyAccessEnabled, FreeBusyAccessLevel, FreeBusyAccessScope, MailTipsAccessEnabled, MailTipsAccessLevel, MailTipsAccessScopeIf results show (1) Enabled: True, and (2) either FreeBusyAccessEnabled: True or MailtipsAccessEnabled: True, and (3) the external organization is hosted in Microsoft 365, your tenant is affected and in scope to migrate. Else, no action is needed. 
    • Get-SharingPolicy | Format-List Name, Domains, Enabled, DefaultIf results show (1) Enabled: True, and (2) the Domains property contains at least one rule with a CalendarSharingFreeBusy access level (Simple, Detail, or Reviewer), and (3) the targeted external organization is hosted in Microsoft 365, and (4) the policy is assigned to one or more mailboxes, your tenant is affected and in scope to migrate. Else, no action is needed.
    • Note: rules that begin with Anonymous: represent calendar publishing to anonymous internet recipients via a published URL - these also appear in this output.

What happens if I do nothing:

Starting October 1, 2026, Exchange Web Services (EWS) will be gradually disabled in line with previous communications linked to this message. As this rollout reaches your tenant, cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing that rely on EWS will be affected — recipients in partner organizations may no longer see Free/Busy, MailTips, or shared calendars from your tenant. 

If your organization is not ready to migrate, you can retain EWS access by following the guidance of the latest blog we published: ExchangeOnline EWS, Your Time is Almost Up (EWSEnabled set to True) while you prepare and execute the migration steps attached to this message. EWS access through this extension will remain available until the final EWS shutdown on April 1, 2027. 

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

  • Follow this Message center post for updates to the rollout schedule. To avoid impact, plan to migrate after the rollout reaches your tenant and before EWS deprecation.
  • Review the migration guide linked below for step-by-step instructions to understand your current configurations, set up new Microsoft 365 Cross Tenant Access Policies, validate the new configurations, and remove unused configurations. 
  • Check the blog post linked below for additional information and answers to frequently asked questions. 
  • Hybrid and on-premises scenarios are not in scope. This update applies to fully cloud-hosted (Exchange Online ↔ Exchange Online) cross-tenant and cross-cloud configurations only. For organizations running on-premises Exchange and Exchange Online in a Hybrid Deployment, migrate to Dedicated Hybrid App. For organizations hosted in Exchange Online sharing with another organization running Exchange on-premises, kindly monitor future Message Center posts for guidance on migration paths as they become available. 

[Additional information:]

  • Migration guide: Migrating to Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy for sharing Free/Busy, Calendars, and MailTips.
  • Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy Microsoft Graph API Overview
  • Exchange Online EWS, Your Time is Almost Up
  • Deprecation of EWS in Exchange Online 
  • Enhancing Microsoft 365 security by eliminating high-privilege access 
  • Blog Post: Cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing are moving to Cross-Tenant Access Policy

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Registration capacity for town halls and webinars increases to 20,000
item.description:
Updated November 23, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

Starting in December, registration capacity for Microsoft Teams town halls and webinars scales with the event's attendee capacity, up to 20,000 registrations per event. Organizers with Teams Enterprise can allow up to 3,000 registrations. Organizers with Attendee Capacity Packs can allow up to 20,000. Organizers can use this to plan large-scale events with registration.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Public Preview: We will begin rolling out on mid-December 2026 and expect to complete by late December 2026.
  • General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in early January 2027 and expect to complete by late January 2027.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizers of Teams town halls and webinars that use registration
  • Admins who manage Teams events policies and Attendee Capacity Pack licenses

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams (town halls and webinars)

What will happen

  • Registration capacity scales with attendee capacity, up to 20,000 registrations per event.
  • Organizers with Teams Enterprise can allow up to 3,000 registrations.
  • Organizers with Attendee Capacity Packs can allow up to 20,000 registrations.
  • Large webinars with registration don't support broadcast-style streaming, which is available with town halls.
  • Organizers still need the right events policy. No new policy access is needed, only the right Attendee Capacity Pack where applicable.
  • Existing Teams events policies and admin controls don't change.
  • We plan to support more registrations per event in future releases.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required. To prepare, you can:

  • Tell organizers about the higher registration limits.
  • Make sure organizers who need more than 3,000 registrations per event have an Attendee Capacity Pack of the right size. Assign packs in the Teams admin center (Add-on Licenses > Teams Events).
  • Update internal training and documentation that mention a 1,000-registration limit.
  • Review your Teams events policies in the Teams admin center (Meetings > Events policies) to confirm they meet your organization's needs.

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: View files and conversations side by side
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Microsoft Teams is introducing a side-by-side experience that helps users review shared files without losing conversation context. When users open a PDF, Markdown, or HTML file from a chat or channel message, the conversation appears alongside the file at the message where it was shared.

This update will be available in Microsoft Teams on Windows, Mac, and the web.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): We will begin rolling out in late December 2026 and expect to complete by early January 2027.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

When users open a supported file from a chat or channel message, a conversation pane opens alongside the file preview. Users can read the related discussion and send messages or replies without leaving the file preview. Files opened from a file list without an originating message will not show the conversation pane.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No admin action is required. Consider notifying help desk staff and end users, and update internal guidance to explain how users can review files and respond to related conversations side by side.

[Compliance considerations:]

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: Expanded Markdown support in the compose box
item.description:
[What and why]

Microsoft Teams is introducing an updated Markdown compose experience with expanded formatting support. Users can write and edit with Markdown syntax intact, without formatting automatically rendering as they type. A dedicated Markdown toolbar helps users insert formatting syntax, preview the rendered message before sending, and switch between Markdown and rich text.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Beginning in early December 2026 and expected to complete by mid-December 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Microsoft Teams users who compose messages in chats and channels on supported platforms

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams for Windows, Mac, and web

What will happen

Users will be able to select Format in Markdown from the compose box’s Actions and apps (+) menu (Screenshot 1).

The updated experience includes:

  • Markdown authoring without live rendering: Syntax remains visible and editable while users write.
  • A dedicated Markdown toolbar: Users can insert syntax for formatting (Screenshot 2).

  • Message preview: Users can turn on Preview message to see the rendered formatting before sending (Screenshot 3).

  • Switching between compose modes: Users can select Format in rich text from the same menu to return to rich text authoring (Screenshot 4).

Teams will remember the user’s selected compose mode and apply it across chats and channels until the user switches modes.

Learn more

  • Use Markdown formatting in Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Support

[Action required and recommendations]

No admin action is required to prepare for this feature.

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: Copilot in channels provides channel-wide context
item.description:
[What and why]

We are introducing a channel-level entry point for Copilot in Microsoft Teams. This enhancement allows users to ask questions and summarize conversations across posts and replies within a channel, rather than a single thread. This enhancement will be available in Microsoft Teams and Teams mobile.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Public Preview (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in early December 2026 and is expected to complete by the end of December 2026.
  • General Availability (Worldwide): We will publish a separate announcement once we've determined a rollout schedule for General Availability.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users of Copilot in Microsoft Teams channels.

Platforms and services

  • Copilot
  • Microsoft Teams
  • Microsoft Teams mobile

What will happen

  • Users can open Copilot from the top-right corner of any Teams channel, ask questions, and generate summaries based on the most recent posts and replies in a channel, rather than a single thread.

  • Copilot responses will include citations that link directly to the source posts or replies.

[Action required and recommendations]

No additional action is required.

[Compliance considerations]

Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI?

  • Yes. This change introduces a new way for users to interact with generative AI in Microsoft Teams by allowing Copilot to answer questions and summarize the most recent posts and replies in a channel.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft 365 Copilot app: New search experience for Microsoft 365 users without a Microsoft 365 Copilot license

item.title: [planForChange] New Contact Support Experience in Outlook for iOS, Android and Mac
item.description:
[What and Why:]

We're introducing a new Contact Support experience in Outlook for iOS, Outlook for Android, and Outlook for Mac. This update brings a more consistent way to get help from within the app, aligned with the Contact Support experience available in new Outlook for Windows.

The existing Contact Support policy for new Outlook, "Allow access to Contact Support in the new Outlook" (outlooknew;L_ContactSupport), will also control Contact Support in Outlook for iOS, Outlook for Android, and Outlook for Mac. No new policy is required.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in late November 2026 and expect to complete by early January 2027.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

The existing Contact Support experience has been replaced with a newer one that improves how users discover solutions for resolving issues on their own. The chat experience provided through Contact Support has not changed, so users can still reach a support agent as they do today. In addition, the Contact Support experience in Outlook for iOS, Outlook for Android and Outlook for Mac now adheres to the same cloud service policy used for New Outlook for Windows.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

Contact Support remains available by default when the policy is enabled or not configured, and administrators who disable the policy will remove access to Contact Support in all of these Outlook clients.

IT admins who have already set the existing policy to "Disabled" will need to redeploy their policy once the updated policy becomes available in the Office Cloud Policy Service (OCPS). Redeploying allows the policy to be updated to include the iOS, Android, and Mac endpoints. If the cloud policy is not redeployed, the Contact Support policy will continue to apply only to new Outlook.

No action is required for organizations that have not configured the policy or have it enabled.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] Sync between Copilot desktop app and Microsoft Edge
item.description:
[What and Why:]

This release adds optional browser data sync between the Copilot desktop app (Windows and Mac) and Microsoft Edge. After opt-in, selected data (passwords, personal info, settings, and browsing history) stays synced across both apps for the signed-in account; payment info is not synced.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-December 2026 and expect to complete by end of December 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

For users, this reduces friction: they can move between Edge and Copilot with familiar browsing data already available, which saves time and improves continuity.

For organizations, it can improve adoption and productivity by lowering setup overhead for users, while still supporting control and transparency because sync is optional, account-based, and excludes payment info.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

Review your browser/data governance posture and decide whether users should be allowed to use this optional sync behavior.

Learn more details will be available when external rollout begins in mid-December.

[Compliance considerations:]

QuestionExplanation
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes - once a user opts in, selected browser data (passwords, personal info, settings, and browsing history) syncs between the Copilot desktop app and Microsoft Edge for the signed-in account. Payment info is explicitly excluded from sync.
Does the change allow a user to enable and disable the feature themselves?Yes - sync is opt-in and account-based; users choose whether to enable it.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Continuous interpreter visibility with pop out video in Teams
item.description:
Updated November 20, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why:]

Users who work with sign language interpreters in Microsoft Teams meetings will be able to pop out their paired interpreters' video into a separate window. The window can be resized and moved anywhere on the screen, including to another monitor. Interpreters stay in view while users multitask, share content, or change meeting layouts. This is designed for Deaf and hard-of-hearing (D/HH) users, for whom losing sight of an interpreter means losing access to the conversation.

[Rollout Schedule:]

Public preview (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out on early December 2026 and expect to complete by late December 2026.

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out on mid January 2027 and expect to complete by late January 2027.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

This applies to Teams desktop on Windows and Mac. After this rollout, users can:

  • Pop out their paired sign language interpreters' video into a dedicated window that stays on top of other apps.
  • Resize the window and move it anywhere on their screen or to another monitor.
  • Keep interpreters in view while presenting, viewing shared content, using chat or captions, or with the main meeting window minimized.

The pop-out window only changes the user's own view, and interpreters stay in the main meeting gallery for everyone else. The window isn't visible to other participants when the user shares their screen.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

You don't need to do anything to prepare. Consider telling D/HH users and the interpreters who support them about this feature, and update your training and accessibility documentation as needed. To use the feature:

  1. In Teams Accessibility settings, turn on Sign language mode and select I am a Signer.
  2. Select Manage interpreters and add the people who interpret for you.
  3. Select View > Pop out interpreters during a meeting.
  4. Users open the pop-out window in each meeting. For faster access, they can pin the Pop out interpreters button to the meeting toolbar. There is no admin policy for this feature.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Copilot: Continue using models after reaching usage limits with Copilot Credits
item.description:
Updated November 20, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why:]

We’re introducing the option to continue using models in Copilot Chat and Office through usage-based billing (UBB) after reaching the usage limits included in a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. After reaching a limit, users can continue with Auto without consuming Copilot Credits or, if they have UBB enabled, can continue with the selected model by consuming Copilot Credits. New credit indicators in the UI help users understand when their work consumes Copilot Credits, while spending policies give administrators control over access and spending.

This capability was originally announced in MC1479276 and is rolling out alongside the models available only through usage-based billing announced in MC1519122.

Additionally, models offered in Chat and Word, Excel, and PowerPoint will now be visible in the model picker. Models that a user does not have access to will be greyed out and users will not be able to select them.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Frontier: Rolling out in early December 2026.
  • General availability: Planned for mid-December 2026 in the Worldwide production cloud.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected: End users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. To use models with usage-based billing in Chat and Word, Excel and PowerPoint, users must also have access to available Copilot Credits through an applicable spending policy that includes the Models with usage-based billing in Chat and Office service.

Platforms/Services: Copilot Chat in the Microsoft Copilot app and Copilot in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint across web, desktop, and mobile.

What will happen:

  • When users reach an applicable model usage limit included in their license, they can continue with Auto without consuming Copilot Credits. Users that have UBB enabled can instead continue with the selected model using Copilot Credits.
  • The new Models with usage-based billing in Chat and Office service will be available in spending policies.
  • Access to models with usage-based billing requires the service to be included in an applicable spending policy, with credits available. Users without this access cannot use models with usage-based billing.
  • Existing spending policies with Auto-apply new services enabled automatically include newly supported services as they become available. Policies with this setting disabled require administrators to add the service.
  • A new credits icon helps users understand credit availability and whether their current experience consumes credits:
    • A filled icon indicates that usage is metered and consumes Copilot Credits.
    • An unfilled icon indicates that usage is not metered and does not consume Copilot Credits.
    • Hovering over the icon shows credit usage details and an option to open a pane with additional information.
  • Users can type and submit /cost as a prompt in Copilot to view details about their current session.
  • Users will see models offered in Chat and Word, Excel, and PowerPoint visible in the model picker. If the user does not have access to a model, it will be greyed out, and the user will not be able to select it.

Image of credit icon and usage details.

Image of banner allowing users to continue with credits if they have UBB enabled.

Action Required/Recommendations:

  1. Review existing spending policies. In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration and review the policies that apply to your users.  
  2. Confirm service access. To allow usage-based model access, ensure the applicable policy includes Models with usage-based billing in Chat and Office, has an appropriate billing method, and has credits available.
  3. Review policy scope, limits, and alerts. Policies can apply to all users or selected Microsoft Entra ID security groups. Confirm the intended audience and configure spending limits and notifications.  
  4. Prepare users and support teams. Explain the choice between Auto and credit-consuming model usage, the new credit indicators, and /cost.

Use these resources to configure and manage access:

  • Set up usage-based billing for Copilot Credits
  • Manage spending policies and service access
  • Monitor Copilot Credit spending

[Compliance considerations:]

New way for end users to interact with generative AIYesEligible users can continue using a selected model after reaching an included usage limit by consuming Copilot Credits.
Administrative control, including Microsoft Entra ID group membershipYesAdministrators control access through service selection in spending policies. Policies support security-group targeting, spending limits, and alerts. [learn.microsoft.com]

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Copilot app: Updates to Home and navigation
item.description:
Updated November 20, 2026: Copilot Workspaces will roll out to standard release in December 2026, and deferred release by January 2027. Thank you for your patience. Refer to MC1559638 for details on Copilot Workspaces.

[What and why]

In MC1479277 about updates to the Microsoft Copilot app, we introduced Home as the new starting point that brings Chat and Cowork together, so users can get chat assistance and delegate multi-step tasks in one view. This post builds on that announcement with worldwide rollout timing and the addition of Projects and Workspaces to the Home experience. 

[Rollout schedule]

  • Standard release begins late October 2026
  • Deferred release begins late November 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users of the Microsoft Copilot app. Access to Cowork and Cowork-related capabilities depends on Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing and your organization’s usage-based billing configuration. 

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Copilot web, desktop, and mobile app.

What will happen

Projects:

  • In addition to what was communicated in MC1479277, Projects provides a dedicated space in Home for organizing related chats, Cowork tasks, and everything they share: files, instructions, and outputs. From there they can create a new project, add files and context, and start chats or Cowork tasks inside it. Responses are grounded in the project's context first, then in the user's broader Microsoft 365 work context. Projects are accessible from the Home navigation pane.
  • Projects doesn't store content itself, and files stay in OneDrive under the same permissions, sensitivity labels and retention policies you already use. Word, Excel and PowerPoint files that Copilot creates are saved to the user's OneDrive.
  • Projects are available on Windows, Mac, & Web apps across tier 1 languages. It is coming soon to mobile apps.

Workspaces:

  • Users will see "Notebooks" become "Workspaces" in the left navigation of the Copilot app as Copilot Notebooks evolves into Copilot Workspaces. Workspaces give teams a shared space to bring together context, team members, and working files to work alongside Copilot on an ongoing workstream.
  • Existing notebooks will convert into “workspaces,” retaining all previously added or made content. Read FAQs on our Support Page.
  • This change will roll out to all users with access to Copilot Notebooks first in the Frontier program. Copilot Workspaces will rollout to standard release in December 2026, and deferred release by January 2027. Access to individual capabilities in Copilot Workspaces will vary by license.

[Action required and recommendations]

  • Review which users are included in a spending policy that grants Cowork access and confirm your intended usage-based billing configuration.

item.title: [stayInformed] Run Python code as a workflow step
item.description:
We are announcing the ability to use the Code node to run Python as a step in a workflow for logic that expressions and connectors cannot handle in Copilot Studio. This feature will reach general availability on December 1, 2026.

How does this affect me?
Makers can add Python steps to workflows for data transforms, file parsing and conversion (e.g. PDF to text, CSV, or XML), and calls to APIs that don't have a connector. The code can be generated using natural language using AI, or Makers can write and edit the code by hand.

Code runs in a Microsoft-managed sandbox environment and consumes Copilot Credits. Code steps are unable to make outbound API calls.

What action do I need to take?
This message is for awareness, and no action is required.

item.title: [stayInformed] Generate documents from the Agent node in workflows
item.description:
We are announcing the ability to generate documents from the Agent node in workflows within Copilot Studio. This feature will reach general availability on December 3, 2026.

How does this affect me?
With this feature, the Agent node can now return files that the agent generates, such as PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and CSV, as workflow outputs.

Key functionality of this feature includes:
  • Ability to work with both inline agents and existing (published) agents.
  • Generated files appear as an ordered files output (name, content type, content) that's available to downstream steps.
  • Ability to pass files to connectors, enabling emailing, saving to SharePoint/OneDrive, and attaching to records.

item.title: [stayInformed] Power Platform - Information regarding the end of support for SharePoint temporary authentication URLs
item.description:
Starting April 1, 2027, SharePoint temporary authentication URLs will no longer be available. Power Apps and Automate functionality that relies on these URLs will break when they are retired.

How does this affect me?
Any Power Apps app or Power Automate cloud flow that relies upon the temporary authentication URLs will stop working.

What action do I need to take?
If you are using only native controls, actions, and connectors, and as long as you are not providing pre-authenticated URLs from SharePoint, then there is no action needed.

If you have authored a custom control, action, or connector with tempauth URLs, then you will need to ensure you have migrated to the new authentication. This may come up in a few ways such as:
  • SharePoint document-library thumbnails not loading
  • SharePoint-stored Images displayed through Image control not loading
  • For the Word Online (Business) connector, CreateWordFileWithContent currently returns a pre-authorized URL that can be used to download the generated document without additional authentication. After temporary authentication is removed, customers should no longer rely on this URL as an unauthenticated file-download mechanism.
After making the required changes, publish updated apps or save and publish updated flows, as applicable. Ensure the updated apps and flows are enabled and tested before the retirement date

For more information on this, visit Pre-authenticated (tempauth) URLs are retiring: move to Microsoft Entra ID tokens before April 1, 2027.

item.title: [stayInformed] Copilot Studio - Create Dataverse agent users with Microsoft Entra agent 's user account
item.description:
We are announcing the ability to create Dataverse agent users with Microsoft Entra agent's user account in Copilot Studio. This feature will reach general availability on December 8th, 2026.

How does this affect me?
This feature enables you to securely deploy agents to access and interact with Dataverse data by using enterprise-managed Microsoft Entra agent identities. The feature ensures agents have only the access required to perform tasks autonomously or on behalf of users. By using identity-based role assignment and full auditing of agent-driven actions, you can enforce security and compliance policies across both human users and agents while maintaining traceability of data access and changes within Dataverse environments.

item.title: [stayInformed] Low-latency alerts and metrics in Monitor
item.description:
We are announcing the ability to evaluate alert rules and review supported metrics for business-critical resources every hour in Monitor, helping admins identify potential issues sooner. This feature will enter public preview on November 23, 2026.

How does this affect me?
When creating or editing an alert rule for a supported app, flow, or agent, admins can set the Data review period to 1 hour. Monitor will evaluate the selected metric after new hourly data becomes available, and the alert can trigger when the configured threshold is crossed. Admins can also switch the metric chart to an hourly view to review activity from the previous 24 hours. These alerts follow an hourly evaluation schedule and are not real-time alerts.

The following products and metrics are supported in the Power Platform admin center experience of Monitor:
  • Canvas and code apps : Time to interactive, app open success rate, data request latency, and data request success rate
  • Model-driven apps : App open success rate
  • Cloud flows : Success rate
  • Copilot Studio agents : Agent session success rate
The following metrics are supported for Copilot Managed Runtime apps in the Microsoft 365 admin center experience of Monitor:
  • Time to interactive
  • App open success rate
  • Data request latency
  • Data request success rate
  • App session count
Low-latency alert rules apply to individual resources and metrics. Only one hourly rule can be configured for each resource and metric, and each tenant can configure up to 10 hourly rules in each supported admin experience. Hourly rules that are turned off continue to count toward this limit. For Power Platform resources, low-latency alerts use resource scope and require the resource to be in a Managed Environment.

What action do I need to take?
This message is for awareness, and no action is required.

If you choose to use this feature, consider configuring hourly alert rules for the business-critical resources where identifying an issue on the same day is most important.

For more information about this feature, please visit:
  • Create alerts for your Power Platform resources
  • Monitor apps in the Microsoft 365 admin center

item.title: [stayInformed] Power Platform Monitor - Route alert notifications to connector-backed destinations
item.description:
We are announcing the ability to route Power Platform Monitor alert notifications to Microsoft Teams, SMS, work item tracking systems, and other connector-backed destinations in Power Platform. This feature will reach public preview on November 20, 2026.

How does this affect me?
Tenant admins can use the new When an alert fires trigger in the Power Platform for Admins V2 connector to create a Power Automate cloud flow that runs when an opted-in Monitor alert fires. The flow can send alert details to any supported connector-backed destination. For example, it can:
  • Post an alert to a Microsoft Teams channel
  • Send an SMS notification
  • Create a work item
  • Perform several of these actions from the same alert
This enables your organization to receive and manage Monitor alerts using the tools and processes your teams already use.

During public preview, this capability supports custom alert rules created in the Power Platform admin center that uses a 24-hour data review period. Support for hourly, low-latency alert rules and environment admins is planned for a future release.

Existing email notifications will continue to function as they do today. Your organization will not experience any changes unless a tenant admin creates a cloud flow using the new trigger.

What action do I need to take?
This message is for awareness, and no action is required.

If you would like more information on this feature, please visit Route alert notifications to any connector-backed destination (preview).

item.title: [stayInformed] Updates to Workforce Insights Agent (Frontier) for Admins in Microsoft 365 Copilot
item.description:
[What and why]

We are adding new capabilities to Workforce Insights Agent (Frontier) in Microsoft 365 Copilot, enabling organizations to get grounded and contextually relevant responses in Copilot from their organizational data. The agent now provides administrators with an additional dedicated workspace to configure organizational definitions, data descriptions and business context. In the agent, admins can also validate how AI reason over those contexts in people and organizational queries and ask the agent to help diagnose gaps or issues where the responses are different than expected.

As the changes rolling out, configurations applied in Workforce Insights Agent will start to apply across some Copilot experiences, with the plan to extend availability across all Copilot experiences in the future. Review the Workforce Insights Agent roadmap and documentation for more details.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Public Preview (Frontier): Beginning in mid-November 2026, the new capabilities will become available to all Frontier tenants

[Impact on Your Organization]

Who is affected

  • Tenants: Tenants with Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses or the Microsoft 365 Copilot in Productivity Apps service plan, and enrolled in Frontier program, will see the agent available in the agent store
  • Administrator roles: Global, AI and Organizational Data Administrators will be needed for configurations

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot, Workforce Insights Agent, Microsoft Entra ID, Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service, and People Skills

What will happen

  • By default, licensed users can discover and install Workforce Insights Agent through Copilot or the Teams agent store, subject to admin policies. This does not grant access to configuration controls or data/expanded scope queries beyond users' existing permissions.
  • AI administrators manage agent deployment and access, while Organizational Data Administrators can configure organizational context and validate results directly in the Workforce Insights Agent. We recommend assigning Organizational Data Administrator to individuals responsible for providing and maintaining data and organizational context, such as HR or People Analytics teams.
  • Workforce Insights Agent uses organizational data from Microsoft Entra ID by default. Organizations can use Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service in Microsoft 365 Admin Center for additional attributes. Configuring context in the agent does not modify data in the underlying source system.
  • In Workforce Insights Agent, administrators can configure organizational context and attribute descriptions to help the agent and soon Copilot better understand how data should be interpreted or metrics should be calculated for your organization. Descriptions explain what each attribute represents, including relevant values, abbreviations, and guidance for its use. With this release, these capabilities apply fully to Workforce Insights Agent and to some types of queries in other Copilot experiences. Check out the Workforce Insights documentation and roadmap for more details and latest updates.

• AI Administrators and Organizational Data Administrators should review deployment scope and configuration for the intended audience.

[Action Required / Recommendations]

Before enabling or expanding use:

  • Review licensing and access: Ensure intended users have the required Microsoft 365 Copilot license, and the tenant has enrolled in Frontier program. Review default discovery and installation. Admins can install the agent for users, restrict access to users or groups, or remove or block it.
  • Prepare data and organizational context: Review Entra ID data quality, reporting relationships, organizational attributes, definitions, and terminology. Additional or replacement data can be provided through Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service. Review permissions and data-handling requirements before uploading. Add organizational context from your existed business collateral to the agent and leverage the interactive tuning experience as appropriate.
  • Review configuration: Admin configurations will move from the Workforce Insights Admin web page to Workforce Insights Agent home page. Supported options include attribute descriptions, organizational context and visibility to all configurations such as attributes & access policies, data access and more.
  • Consider People Skills: Enable People Skills if skills-based queries are required and review its setup and governance requirements.
  • Review data access: Users can request expanded data scope from people with direct reports. Use the WorkforceInsights PowerShell module to control this access according to organizational policies.
  • Validate results: Have authorized users test representative prompts against known data and definitions, address discrepancies, and repeat validation after changes.

Learn more 

  • Workforce Insights Agent
  • Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service
  • People Skills overview
  • Workforce Insights

[Compliance considerations]

Workforce Insights Agent is not designed for behavioral monitoring, performance management or employment decisions. Administrators are responsible for local legal and business requirements, data protection obligations and Works Council guidelines. Configure available controls to align with these requirements and business practices.

Alters processing of existing customer dataProcesses organizational data to generate workforce insights such as structure, roles, and composition.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Teams: Tenant policy controls who can record and transcribe
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Teams administrators can use a policy to configure who may start recording and transcription. The policy supports two participant scopes: organizers and co-organizers, or organizers, co-organizers, and presenters. For each scope, administrators can specify whether meeting organizers can or cannot change the setting.

This provides a centrally managed default or enforced restriction for meetings organized by users assigned the policy, reducing the need for per-meeting configuration.

[Rollout Schedule:]

Targeted Release (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-December 2026 and expect to complete by mid-December 2026.

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in late December 2026 and expect to complete by late December 2026.

General Availability (GCC): We will begin rolling out in late December 2026 and expect to complete by late January 2027.

General Availability (GCC High): We will begin rolling out in mid-February 2027 and expect to complete by late February 2027.

General Availability (DoD): We will begin rolling out in mid-February 2027 and expect to complete by early March 2027.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

A new Who can record and transcribe policy control will be available in the Recording & transcription section of the applicable Teams meeting policy in the Teams admin center.

The default value is Organizers, co-organizers, and presenters. Organizers can change, which preserves the current behavior.

Administrators can select one of the following four options in a single dropdown:

Who can record and transcribe - policy optionBehavior
Organizers and co-organizers. Organizers can changeDefaults to organizers and co-organizers. Organizers can also allow presenters through the existing meeting option.
Organizers and co-organizers. Organizers can't changeLocks the policy value. Presenters and attendees cannot start recording or transcription.
Organizers, co-organizers, and presenters. Organizers can changeDefaults to organizers, co-organizers, and presenters. Organizers can restrict the roles through the existing meeting option.
Organizers, co-organizers, and presenters. Organizers can't changeLocks the policy value. The organizer cannot change the role selection.

These configurations remain subject to existing recording and transcription availability controls and any sensitivity label that configures this option.

  • Enforcement: When organizer changes are blocked, Meeting options shows the policy value as read-only with a notice that it is locked by meeting policy. The effective role restriction is also enforced when a participant tries to start recording or transcription.
  • Sensitivity labels and templates: A sensitivity label that configures this option takes precedence over the meeting policy. A locked meeting policy takes precedence over a meeting template. An unlocked policy supplies a default.
  • Related meeting options: The existing Who can record and transcribe meeting option remains a Teams Premium or Microsoft 365 Copilot feature.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

  • No action is required. If you do not configure the new policy, existing recording and transcription behavior remains unchanged.
  • If your organization needs to prevent presenters from starting recording or transcription, consider using the new Who can record and transcribe policy.
  • Review policy assignments, sensitivity labels, and meeting templates to confirm the effective behavior.
  • Notify meeting organizers and helpdesk teams of any changes and update internal guidance.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Enhanced prompt categories for Microsoft 365 Copilot in Microsoft Copilot Dashboard and Agent 365 Business Analytics
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Enhanced prompt categories for Microsoft 365 Copilot provide a detailed view into Copilot Chat usage by users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. Copilot Chat prompts are classified into 13 categories and 41 subcategories, which show how users apply Copilot Chat in their work. The enhanced categories replace the four legacy prompt categories in the Microsoft Copilot Dashboard: "Ask and find," "Catch up," "Draft and brainstorm" and "Other."

With this update, leaders and adoption teams can:

  • See how users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license use Copilot Chat across categories such as finding information, analyzing content, writing and creating content, summarizing content, and more.
  • Break down active users and prompts by category for groups, organizations and job functions, using your existing Copilot Dashboard and Agent 365 business analytics filters.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out on mid December 2026 and expect to complete by end of December 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

The four legacy categories are being retired. "Ask and find," "Catch up," "Draft and brainstorm" and "Other" will be removed from the Copilot Dashboard and replaced by the enhanced categories.

Enhanced prompt categories apply to Copilot Chat usage by users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. Usage of Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat by users without a Microsoft 365 Copilot license isn't included.

You'll find the new categories in these places:

Microsoft Copilot Dashboard

  • Adoption tab: Shows the number and percentage of Copilot Chat users in each category.
  • Impact tab: Shows the number and percentage of prompts in each category.

Agent 365 Business Analytics

  • Use cases page: Treemap view of categories and subcategories, breakdown table by prompt category, heatmap by job function, organization, or group.

The dashboard uses the same prompt category names across tenants; no user input prompt text is shown.

Anyone who already has Copilot Dashboard or Agent 365 business analytics can view the enhanced prompt categories. There's no separate setting to configure. This change is on by default.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

We recommend that you update guidance and training materials that refer to the legacy categories. No admin action is required.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] Copilot video creation in Clipchamp Video Hub is now live in Frontier Public
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Copilot video creation is coming to the Clipchamp Video Hub. It turns documents, ideas and work content into videos that make complex information easier to understand and act on. Users start with a prompt, a document from OneDrive, or relevant work context, then preview the video in chat and refine it through conversation until they’re happy with it.

This is a usage-based billing (UBB) feature. Each video and subsequent refinements use Copilot Credits, billed through Copilot Credits usage-based billing in the Microsoft 365 admin center. To enable access, admins must enable Anthropic models and configure Copilot Credits spending policies for intended users.

Key features:

  • Create from a prompt. Describe the topic, audience, tone and length, or pick a starter prompt. 
  • Create in your language. Describe the video in your preferred language and make localized content for audiences worldwide. 
  • Base videos on your content. Add a Word document, PowerPoint presentation, images, video or PDF from OneDrive, or draw on relevant work context through Work IQ. 
  • Refine through conversation. Ask for changes like "Use a more formal tone", "Make it shorter", "Localize this into Japanese" or "Update the title." 
  • Preview in chat. Watch each version without leaving the experience. 
  • Export and share. Save the finished video as an MP4. 

How to get started: 

Admins first turn on Copilot video creation in a spending policy that includes the right users, in Copilot > Cost management in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

Users can then:

  • Open Clipchamp Video Hub 
    • [CompanyName].sharepoint.com/_layouts/15/videohub.aspx?vhnav=video-agent-home
  • Go to Create video in the left menu
  • Describe the video, and add files if needed.
  • Preview the video, refine it.
  • Select Export to save it as an MP4.

[Rollout Schedule:]

Public Preview (Frontier public): available as of November 17, 2026.

General Availability (Worldwide): Expected February (timing subject to final confirmation).

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Users included in eligible spending policies can create and refine videos from work content in Clipchamp Video Hub. Video creation and refinements consume Copilot Credits and appear in Copilot cost management reporting. 

Governance:

  • Exported videos carry a "Made with AI" watermark, which admins can turn off. 
  • Videos only draw on work content the user already has access to.

Known limitations at preview:

  • Sensitivity labels: Videos created from documents with a sensitivity label above General can't be downloaded yet but can be viewed.
  • Availability: Anthropic models must be enabled for your organization. If they're turned off, video creation isn't available.
  • Generation: Creating and changing videos can take some time. Requests may sometimes fail or time out, and preview or playback may not work as expected.
  • Editing: Changes happen through conversation, and videos export as MP4. Editing individual scenes or elements in Clipchamp isn't supported yet.
  • Source material: WorkIQ, Web search, Word, PowerPoint, images (up to 3 per prompt), Videos (under 50mb) and PDF are supported. More file types and multiple sources will come in future releases.
  • Sessions: Keep the browser tab open while a video is being created. Only one session at a time is supported.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Enhanced Copilot and AI controls for meetings
item.description:
Updated November 19, 2026: We have updated the content. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why:]

Microsoft Teams is updating how administrators and meeting organizers configure AI for Teams meetings. The existing Copilot meeting policy is being replaced by two more specific policies:

  • MeetingAI - controls whether Copilot, Facilitator, Intelligent Recap, and other AI features are available in meetings.
  • TranscriptionWithMeetingAI - controls whether transcription starts automatically when meeting AI is turned on.

This gives administrators clearer, more predictable control over whether AI is available and whether it requires (or works without) transcription, including the ability to enforce Copilot off. Organizers also gain more visibility into, and in some cases control over, these settings directly from the meeting options.

Meeting options are also being updated to make AI controls easier to understand and to provide more granular control over who can enable, manage, and use AI capabilities, including a new who can manage option that replaces the existing Allow Copilot and Facilitator meeting option:

  • Who can manage AI - replaces the existing Allow Copilot and Facilitator option and determines who can turn Copilot and other AI features on or off during a meeting. If an admin turns Meeting AI off, this option is set to No one.
  • Who can use AI - provides more granular control over which meeting participants can use Copilot and other AI capabilities.
  • Start Transcription with AI - lets organizers choose whether transcription starts with AI. Administrators can also control this option through Teams admin center.
  • Intelligent Recap controls - lets organizers decide whether an Intelligent Recap is created when Copilot is turned on, including for meetings where a transcript is not created.

[Rollout Schedule:]

Targeted Release (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in early December 2026 (previously mid-November) and expect to complete by mid-December 2026 (previously early December).

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in early January 2027 (previously late November 2026) and expect to complete by mid-January 2027 (previously early December 2026).

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Today, the Copilot policy combines whether AI is available in a meeting with whether a saved transcript is required. After this update, these behaviors are represented by two separate settings:

  • Allow AI in meetings: On / Off, but organizers can change / Off, and organizers cannot change
  • Start transcription when AI is turned on: On, but organizers can change / On, and organizers cannot change / Off

To keep the experience predictable and avoid invalid combinations: if MeetingAI is set to enforced off, transcription will also be turned off; if transcription is then turned back on, MeetingAI will no longer be enforced off.

In PowerShell, administrators will use MeetingAI and TranscriptionWithMeetingAI instead of the existing Copilot policy. Once the new controls are enabled, the Copilot policy can no longer be updated directly - attempts will return guidance to use the new policies.

What happens to existing configurations: Microsoft will perform a one-time update mapping each existing Copilot value to the corresponding MeetingAI and TranscriptionWithMeetingAI values, preserving the current effective behavior for your organization. Administrators do not need to recreate their policies. Examples include:

Existing configurationMeetingAITranscriptionWithMeetingAI
Copilot is on and uses a saved transcript by defaultOnOn, but organizers can change
Copilot is on and a saved transcript is requiredOnOn, and organizers cannot change
Copilot is available without transcriptionOnOff
Copilot is off, but organizers can enable itOff, but organizers can changeBased on the existing transcription configuration
Copilot is enforced offOff, and organizers cannot changeOff

The Transcription policy remains available and continues to control whether transcription is allowed. The new TranscriptionWithMeetingAI policy controls whether transcription starts when meeting AI is turned on.

The new settings will appear in the Teams admin center meeting policy under Recording and transcription and Copilot and other AI:

Screenshot 1 - Teams Admin Center: Meeting Policies

Screenshot 2 - Meeting options: Recording & Transcription 

Screenshot 3 - Meeting options: Copilot and other AI

Screenshot 4 - Teams Admin Center: Meeting Templates

These screenshots show the new Start transcription when AI is turned on control and Allow AI in all meetings control, including the Teams Admin Center options administrators can use to set defaults or prevent organizers from changing the configured behavior.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No admin action is required to migrate existing configurations. Before rollout, we recommend admins:

  • Review any automation or scripts that read or update the Copilot meeting policy, and update them to use MeetingAI and TranscriptionWithMeetingAI.
  • Review custom tooling, runbooks, or documentation referencing the Copilot policy.
  • Inform Teams administrators that existing behavior will now be represented by two settings in Teams admin center.
  • Confirm the mapped configuration reflects intended behavior once the new controls are available.

If you do not use PowerShell or custom automation to manage Teams meeting policies, no action is required. Existing configurations will be mapped automatically.

[Compliance considerations:]

This change affects administrative controls over AI and transcription availability in meetings but does not alter how existing customer data is processed or stored. Review AI and transcription governance policies for your organization as appropriate.

item.title: [preventOrFixIssue] (Updated) Microsoft Entra ID: Risk-based anti-bot verification (CAPTCHA) for SMS and voice multi-factor authentication
item.description:
Updated November 19, 2026: We have updated the content. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

Microsoft Entra ID is adding safeguards to protect telephony-based multifactor authentication (MFA) from automated fraudulent activity. Some users who use SMS or voice for MFA may be asked to complete a risk-based anti-bot verification step (CAPTCHA) before Microsoft sends an SMS verification code or initiates a verification call.

If your organization has restrictive network or firewall settings, make sure to follow the guidance covered in this documentation (Risk-based anti-bot verification (CAPTCHA) for telephony-based sign-in - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn) to prepare for this change.

This change is separate from the planned retirement of SMS and voice authentication and does not affect the retirement timeline.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Worldwide: Beginning in mid-November 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users who use SMS or voice for Microsoft Entra ID multifactor authentication

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra ID
  • SMS and voice authentication methods

What will happen

  • Some users may be prompted to complete a risk-based anti-bot verification step (CAPTCHA) before Microsoft sends an SMS verification code or initiates a verification call.
  • The verification step will appear only for authentication attempts that meet sufficiently high-risk thresholds.
  • Users with restrictive network or firewall settings may be unable to complete SMS or voice MFA if the verification experience cannot load.

[Action required and recommendations]

We recommend that administrators take the following actions:

  • Prepare your help desk and notify users that some SMS and voice MFA attempts may require an additional CAPTCHA verification step.
  • Review the risk-based anti-bot verification documentation for network-readiness guidance. If your organization uses restrictive firewalls, proxies, or web filtering, ensure that the required resources can load during authentication.
  • Continue moving users to phishing-resistant authentication methods, such as passkeys, where possible.

Learn more

  • Risk-based anti-bot verification (CAPTCHA) for telephony-based sign-in - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn
  • Understanding telephony fraud risk for Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn
  • Passkeys by default and retirement of Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Unified management of app and agent availability and installation in Teams, Outlook, and the Microsoft 365 app
item.description:
Updated November 18, 2026: Unified app and agent installation management is now generally available. For any tenant that unifies app/agent availability through Phase 1, Phase 2, or Phase 3, app and agent installations are also unified across the Microsoft 365 admin center (MAC) and Teams admin center (TAC) within 24–48 hours of completing availability unification.

What it is

Microsoft is rolling out a new feature to streamline how app and agent availability and installation is managed across Teams, Outlook, and Microsoft 365 Copilot. Until now, IT admins configured availability and installation settings separately in both the Microsoft 365 Admin Center (MAC) and the Teams Admin Center (TAC), which led to mismatches. With this update, you’ll be able to unify availability and installation policies for apps and agents across both portals, making app management more consistent and efficient.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 393931, 485712 and 503105.

When this will happen: 

  • App and agent availability unification (Section A): Rollout began in late September 2025. The Phase 3 timeline will be announced separately, at least 60 days before that phase begins.
  • App and agent installation unification (Section B): Released. Installation unification completes within 24–48 hours after a tenant completes app availability unification(Section A) in Phase 1, 2, or 3

A: Unify app availability across admin centers

1. Phase 1 – Default Tenant Unification of App/Agent Availability

We will begin rolling out this feature at the end of September 2025. This initial phase targets tenants that have never modified their organization-wide defaults, app availability, or block/unblock in either the Microsoft 365 admin center or the Teams admin center. At the end of this phase, agent and app manageability will be unified across both Microsoft 365 admin center and Teams admin center ensuring agent and Microsoft 365 apps availability policies are in alignment for all future administrative changes. This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 393931.

2.Phase 2 – Modified Tenants Unification of App/Agent Availability

This phase targets tenants that have previously modified their organization-wide defaults, app availability, or block/unblock settings in either admin center. These tenants will be transitioned to a unified management experience across both Microsoft 365 and Teams admin centers.

  • For tenants with no agent or app availability differences across both admin centers, guidance will be provided to help maintain unified availability policy for all future changes.

For tenants with agent or app availability differences across both admin centers, a wizard in the Teams admin center will help identify affected agents and apps and guide through resolving discrepancies.

  • As part of this phase we will also enable administrators to manage Microsoft 365 certified SaaS applications within their tenant through org-wide settings for third-party apps. This has been rolled out completely for all tenants.
  • This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 485712 & 503105.

This phase has been fully rolled out to all tenants. Tenants can choose to align through the wizard experience available in Teams admin center.

Note: In this phase, no changes will be applied to org-wide settings or app-level settings without administrator action.

3. Phase 3 – Automatic Unification (Future)

Tenants that have not taken action to unify availability through the wizard experience released in Phase 1 and Phase 2 will have their availability automatically unified across MAC and TAC as part of this phase. We will inform customers of the timeline and additional details at least 60 days in advance before this phase begins.

B: Unified app and agent installation management 

This capability unifies installation management across the Teams admin center and Microsoft 365 admin center. Administrators can manage supported app and agent installations from either portal, with changes synchronized across both admin centers. 

Who receives this capability? 

Tenants whose app and agent availability has been unified through any of the phases described in section A are eligible. Once rollout begins, this capability will be automatically enabled for tenants whose availability is already unified as part of Section A. Tenants that unify their availability later will receive this capability automatically once unified. 

Note: This capability is separate from availability unification described in section A . It does not automatically unify app or agent availability. 

When will it roll out? 

Rollout will begin at the end of September 2026 for eligible tenants. This date applies only to installation management (section B). 

Is administrator action required? 

No additional action is required to enable installation unification for eligible tenants. Existing installation assignments for supported apps and agents will be synchronized across both admin centers. 

Important: App installation is no longer managed through Teams app setup policies. Installations previously made through those policies are not unified as part of this change.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: Real-time queue metrics in the Queues app on Mobile

We're introducing real-time call queue metrics in the Queues app on Microsoft Teams Mobile. Calling representatives and supervisor leads can now monitor key operational metrics directly from their mobile devices, giving them greater visibility into queue activity and performance while on the go.

Users can quickly understand the state of their queues, monitor incoming call demand, and make informed decisions about their availability and queue participation without needing to switch to desktop.

  • Stay informed about queue performance: Access operational metrics for their assigned call queues without switching to desktop.
  • Make informed decisions: Use real-time queue information to better understand call demand and manage their availability and queue participation.

The metrics available to users will depend on their role and existing permissions. Calling representatives will have visibility into the metrics available to them, while supervisor leads will have access to additional queue information based on their permissions.

This feature extends the existing real-time queue metrics experience to Mobile and does not change how call queues are configured or managed.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]
